full_name_ar: هانئ بن عبد الله بن الشخير
bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (vol. 30, p. 140, entry 6544) lists Hani' ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir (ibn 'Awf ibn Ka'b ibn Waqdan ibn al-Huraysh) al-'Amiri al-Harashi al-Basri, brother of Mutarrif and Yazid ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir and father of 'Abdullah ibn Hani'. He narrated from his father 'Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir, and Abu Bishr Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyya narrated from him. Ibn Hibban lists him in al-Thiqat. Al-Nasa'i transmitted his hadith about the Prophet telling a traveller that God has lifted fasting and half the prayer from the traveller. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: هانئ أبو سعيد البربري الدمشقي
bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (vol. 30, p. 147, entry 6550) lists Hani', Abu Sa'id al-Barbari, client (mawla) of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, who owned a house in Damascus near Suq al-Ahad. He narrated from Juray ibn al-Harith (client of 'Umar) and from his master 'Uthman ibn 'Affan; Sulayman (or 'Umar) ibn Yathribi and Abu Wa'il 'Abdullah ibn Buhayr ibn Raysan al-Qass narrated from him. Al-Nasa'i said 'no harm in him'; Ibn Hibban lists him in al-Thiqat. Ibn Sa'd says he had lost his sight and that after 'Uthman's killing his descendants affiliated themselves to Hamdan. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmitted his hadith. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: هرمي بن عبد الله
bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (vol. 30, p. 165, entry 6560) lists Harmi ibn 'Abdullah (also said Harmi ibn 'Utba, Harmi ibn 'Amr, or 'Abdullah ibn Harmi) al-Ansari al-Waqifi, or al-Khatmi, of Medina, whose companion status is disputed. He has a single hadith from Khuzayma ibn Thabit prohibiting intercourse with women in the anus, with major disturbance (idtirab) in its chain. Thumama ibn Qays al-Waqifi, Husayn ibn Mihsan al-Khatmi, Humayd ibn Qays al-A'raj, 'Abdullah ibn 'Ali ibn al-Sa'ib, 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Amr al-Khatmi and others narrated from him. The next page notes Ibn Sa'd's and Ibn Makula's remarks on his lineage, that he was among those who wept when the Prophet prepared for Tabuk, and that al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah transmitted from him. No death year is given.

He narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam, Sa'id al-Maqburi, Safwan ibn Sulaym, Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, Yazid ibn Ruman, his father 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira and others; Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hunayni, Ayyub ibn Salama al-Ghifari and Khalid ibn Makhlad al-Qatawani narrated from him. Critics were severe: Ahmad ibn Hanbal called him weak in hadith, Abu Hatim said weak and very munkar, al-Bukhari said his hadiths are almost nothing, and al-Nasa'i called him matruk and not trustworthy. Ibn Majah transmitted one hadith of his from Yazid ibn Ruman from Abu Hurayra. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: أبو ماجد
bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 7596) lists Abu Majida, also called Abu Majid, al-Hanafi al-'Ijli al-Kufi; Abu Hatim gives his name as 'A'idh ibn Nadla. He narrated from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani and Yahya ibn 'Abdullah al-Jabir narrated from him. Critics were harsh: al-Bukhari and others recorded him as munkar al-hadith, al-Tirmidhi called him majhul, al-Nasa'i munkar al-hadith, and al-Daraqutni majhul and matruk. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmitted his hadith from Ibn Mas'ud on walking with the funeral procession. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: محمد بن طلحة بن عبيد الله القرشي التيمي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 7797, starting at shamela.ws/book/9767/2979) lists him as Muhammad ibn Talha ibn 'Ubaydullah al-Qurashi al-Taymi, son of Talha (one of the ten promised Paradise); al-Bukhari counted him among the Companions and he was born in the Prophet's lifetime. The entry reports (via Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Talha) that the Prophet named him and gave him the kunya Abu al-Qasim. He was devoted to worship and was called al-Sajjad. At the Battle of the Camel he sheathed his sword on 'A'isha's advice and was killed by Shurayh ibn Awfa; 'Ali passed by and said 'this is al-Sajjad, his devotion to his father killed him', in the year 36 AH.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 8325, second section of the letter Mim) lists him as Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf al-Zuhri. Citing Ibn Sa'd's Tabaqat, it says she married Makhrama ibn Nawfal and bore him al-Miswar, Safwan al-Akbar, al-Salt al-Akbar and Umm Safwan; she and her sister al-Shifa' bint 'Awf embraced Islam and pledged allegiance to the Prophet, and Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) counts both sisters among the emigrant women. No death year is given.

full: 'Afra' bint 'Ubayd b. Tha'laba b. 'Ubayd b. Tha'laba b. Ghanm b. Malik b. al-Najjar

Ibn Habib counts her among the women who pledged allegiance to the Prophet. She was the mother of Mu'adh, Mu'awwidh and 'Awf, sons of al-Harith, each known as Ibn 'Afra'. Ibn Sa'd says her mother was al-Ru'a bint 'Adi ibn Mu'adh and that she married al-Harith ibn Rifa'a ibn al-Harith ibn Sawad; the entry notes she was distinguished by having seven sons who all fought at Badr. No death year is given.

full: Fadala bin 'Adi bin Haram b. al-Haythum b. Zafar b. al-Khazraj b. 'Amr b. Malik b. al-Aus
full_name_ar: فضالة بن عدي الأنصاري الظفري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 7008, marked as an addition) lists him as Fadala ibn 'Adi al-Ansari al-Zafari, grandfather of Muhammad ibn Anas ibn Fadala. Ibn Manda stated in Muhammad's biography that both Anas and Fadala were Companions, but omitted a separate entry for Fadala, which Abu Musa supplied. Al-Baghawi transmitted a hadith through Yunus ibn Muhammad ibn Fadala from his father stating that his father and grandfather accompanied the Prophet; Ibn Hajar notes the chain properly runs through Idris ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus ibn Muhammad ibn Anas ibn Fadala. The editor cites Usd al-Ghaba and al-Tarikh al-Saghir. No death year is given.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 156) lists al-Aswad ibn Khalaf ibn As'ad ibn 'Amir ibn Bayada al-Khuza'i, matching our Arabic name field (the English 'famous' field names his son Muhammad ibn al-Aswad, but the page entry is about al-Aswad himself). Khalifa ibn Khayyat counted him among the Companions, and Ibn Hibban said he is reported to have had companionship, with some doubt about the chain. Ibn Hajar notes that Ibn Sa'd confused him with a different al-Aswad ibn Khalaf ibn 'Abd Yaghuth al-Qurashi (entry 157), and that al-Dhahabi did not clearly separate the two, though they are distinct individuals. bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5098, first section of the letter 'Ayn) lists him as 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Umayya ibn Abi 'Ubayda ibn Hammam al-Tamimi, an ally (halif) of Quraysh and brother of Ya'la ibn Umayya (known as Ibn Munya). 'Abd al-Razzaq transmits a report (via Ibn Jurayj and 'Amr ibn Dinar from Abu Ya'la ibn Umayya from his father) that 'Abd al-Rahman bought a horse for a hundred young camels and the seller complained to 'Umar that Ya'la and his brother had wrongfully taken the horse. Ibn Hajar adds that a Qurashi or their ally who lived in the Prophet's time would have attended the Farewell Pilgrimage. No death year is given.

Ibn Hibban lists him in Thiqat al-Tabi'in, and al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh says he heard from 'Umar. No death year is given.

'Uthman appointed him governor of Basra in 29 AH after Abu Musa al-Ash'ari; during his governorship Khurasan, parts of Persia, Sijistan and Kerman were conquered and the Persian king Yazdegerd was killed. The entry (continued on the next page) says he died in the year 57 or 58 AH.

full: Hawwa', the grandmother of 'Amr bin Mu'adh al-Ansari
full_name_ar: حواء جدة عمرو بن معاذ الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (women's section, entry 11071) has an entry for Hawwa', known as Umm Bujayd al-Ansariyya, whose hadith Malik transmits from Zayd ibn Aslam from Umm Bujayd from her grandmother from the Prophet: 'Give something to the beggar, even a burnt hoof.' Ahmad records the same in his Musnad via Rawh ibn 'Ubada from Malik and titles her 'Hawwa', grandmother of 'Amr ibn Mu'adh'. Another version via Sa'id al-Maqburi has 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bujayd al-Ansari narrating from his grandmother Hawwa'. Ibn Hajar notes Ibn Manda confused her with a different Hawwa' (bint Yazid vs. bint Zayd). No death year is given.

full: Salama bint al-Hurr b. Qays b. Hasan b. Hudhayfa b. Badr al-Fazariyya or al-Zadiyya
full_name_ar: سلامة بنت الحر الفزارية ( رضي الله عنها
bio: Entry 3378 in Ibn 'Abd al-Barr's al-Isti'ab (women's section): Salama bint al-Hurr, called al-Asadiyya, or al-Azdiyya, or al-Fazariyya, sister of Kharasha bin al-Hurr. She narrated several hadiths from the Prophet, including 'there will be among Thaqif a liar and a destroyer' and 'a time will come upon people when they stand for an hour and find no one to lead them in prayer'. Waki' and Umm Dawud al-Wabishiyya transmitted from her. No dates are given.

bio: Entry 777 in Ibn 'Abd al-Barr's al-Isti'ab: Rifa'a bin Samaw'al (also called Rifa'a bin Rifa'a) al-Qurazi, of Banu Qurayza. He is identified as the man who divorced his wife three times in the Prophet's time, after which 'Abd al-Rahman bin al-Zubayr married and divorced her before consummation; the entry notes this hadith is established in al-Muwatta' and elsewhere, and cites him saying a Qur'anic verse was revealed concerning ten men of whom he was one. His son narrated from him. No dates are given.
research_evidence: رفاعة بن سموأل ويقال رفاعة بن رفاعة القرظي، من بنى قريظة

bio: Entry 1966 in al-Mizzi's Tahdhib al-Kamal: al-Zubayr bin 'Abd al-Rahman bin al-Zubayr bin Bata al-Qurazi al-Madani. He narrated from his father, and al-Miswar bin Rifa'a al-Qurazi narrated from him. His one hadith concerns Rifa'a bin Samaw'al al-Qurazi divorcing his wife Tamima bint Wahb three times in the Prophet's lifetime; al-Nasa'i recorded it via Yunus bin 'Abd al-A'la from Ibn Wahb and judged the correct form to be mursal. Ibn Hibban listed him in al-Thiqat. No death year is given.
research_evidence: الزبير بن عبد الرحمن بن الزبير بن باطا القرظي المدني

bio: Entry 2648 in Ibn 'Abd al-Barr's al-Isti'ab (cross-referenced from entry 2143, Qays bin 'Abdullah bin 'Amr bin 'Udus ... bin Ja'da): al-Nabigha al-Ja'di the poet, whose given name is disputed (Qays bin 'Abdullah, or a lineage beginning Hibban bin Qays). He composed poetry in the Jahiliyya, fell silent for about thirty years, then resumed, hence the name al-Nabigha; he is said to be older than al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani and to have kept company with al-Nu'man bin al-Mundhir. He came to the Prophet as a Muslim and recited poetry to him, and the Prophet prayed for him. He is reported to have lived 180 or, per Ibn Qutayba, 220 years, and died in Isfahan. No death year is given.
research_evidence: النابغة الجعدي ... قديما شاعرا محسنا طويل البقاء في الجاهلية والإسلام ... عمر النابغة الجعدي مائتين وعشرين سنة، ومات بأصبهان

bio: Abu Nu'aym al-Isbahani's Ma'rifat al-Sahaba gives an entry for Ahmar bin Jaz' al-Sadusi al-Rab'i, tracing his lineage through Tha'laba bin Zayd bin Malik bin Sinan, and counts him among the Basrans. Only al-Hasan (al-Basri) transmitted from him. The entry says he was given the kunya Abu Shu'ayl by al-Mani'i, which Abu Nu'aym considers an error. No dates are given.

Abu Nu'aym's Ma'rifat al-Sahaba (shamela.ws/book/10490/1329) likewise has 'al-Adra' al-Aslami' and says he used to stand guard for the Prophet. No dates are given.

full_name_ar: أهبان بن أوس الأسلمى ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Entry 99 in Ibn 'Abd al-Barr's al-Isti'ab: Ahban bin Aws al-Aslami, kunya Abu 'Uqba, was one of the 'companions of the tree' at al-Hudaybiya. He built a house in Kufa and died there in the early days of Mu'awiya's rule. The entry notes that some say the 'one who spoke with the wolf' (mukallim al-dhi'b) was Ahban bin 'Iyadh instead. No exact death year is given.

bio: Entry 100 in Ibn 'Abd al-Barr's al-Isti'ab: Ahban bin Sayfi al-Ghifari, a Basran with the kunya Abu Muslim. When 'Ali came to Basra he asked Ahban why he had stayed out of the fighting; Ahban replied that the Prophet had told him that when the community split into two factions he should take a sword of wood. The entry also relates, on the authority of a group of reliable Basrans, a report about his burial shroud. No death year is given.
research_evidence: أهبان بن صيفي الغفاري البصري ... إذا تفرقت الأمة فرقتين فاتخذ سيفا من خشب

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 730) lists him as Bakr ibn Mubashshir ibn Jabr al-Ansari al-Awsi. Abu Hatim and Ibn Hibban affirm his companionship, Ibn Hibban adding that he is counted among the people of Medina. Ibn al-Sakan says he has one hadith with a sound chain, which al-Hakim (Mustadrak), Abu Dawud, al-Bukhari (Tarikh) and al-Bawardi transmitted. Ibn al-Qattan notes only Ishaq ibn Salim narrated from him. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: الحكم بن سفيان ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 1783) lists him as al-Hakam ibn Sufyan ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Amir ibn Mu'attib al-Thaqafi. Abu Zur'a and Ibrahim al-Harbi affirm his companionship; his hadith on sprinkling water after wudu is transmitted by the Sunan compilers via Mujahid, with disagreement over whether the name is al-Hakam ibn Sufyan or Sufyan ibn al-Hakam. Ahmad and al-Bukhari denied he was a companion. No death year is given.

No death year is given.

His son 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jarhad and grandson Zur'a ibn Muslim ibn Jarhad narrated from him. Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba (entry 1134, shamela.ws/book/9767/565) gives the lineage Jarhad ibn Khuwaylid ... ibn Razah al-Aslami, counts him among Ahl al-Suffa, credits him with the hadith that the thigh is 'awra, and says he died in Medina at the end of Yazid's caliphate.

Al-Ash'ath ibn 'Amr, al-Sa'ib ibn Malik and al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mina' narrated from him; his hadith appears in Abu Dawud's al-Marasil and Ibn Majah. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: الحارث بن خفاف ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 1406) lists al-Harith ibn Khufaf ibn Ayma' ibn Rahada al-Ghifari. Ibn Hajar infers his companionship from a report in Sahih al-Bukhari (via Aslam from 'Umar) in which 'Umar says he saw the father and brother of Khufaf's daughter besieging a fortress; since Khufaf's only recorded sons were Mikhlad (a famous tabi'i) and al-Harith, 'Umar's remark must refer to al-Harith. No death year is given.

No death year is given.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2406) lists Dukayn ibn Sa'id (or Sa'd) al-Khath'ami, also said to be al-Muzani. He has a single hadith, transmitted only by Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, and is counted among the companions who settled in Kufa. His hadith is recorded by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, Abu Dawud, and al-Daraqutni in al-Ilzamat. No death year is given.
research_evidence: دكين: بالكاف مصغرا، ابن سعيد أو سعد الخثعميّ. ويقال المزني. له حديث واحد تفرد أبو إسحاق السّبيعي بروايته عنه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Sharhabayl (or 'Uthman) bin al-A'war b. 'Amr b Mua'wiya
full_name_ar: ذو الجوشن بفتح ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2455) lists Dhu al-Jawshan al-Dibabi, whose name is given as Aws ibn al-A'war (per al-Marzubani), Shurahbil ibn al-A'war ibn 'Amr ibn Mu'awiya (the better known), or 'Uthman ibn Nawfal (per Ibn Shahin); Dibab is a branch of Kilab ibn Rabi'a ibn 'Amir ibn Sa'sa'a. Muslim affirms his companionship. Ibn al-Athir says he was nicknamed Dhu al-Jawshan because Khosrow gave him a breastplate (jawshan) which he wore. He was a horseman and poet with fine elegies for his brother al-Sumayl, and has a hadith in Abu Dawud via Abu Ishaq. No death year is given.
research_evidence: ذو الجوشن الضّبابيّ: قيل: اسمه أوس بن الأعور. وبه جزم المرزبانيّ، وقيل شرحبيل- وهو الأشهر- ابن الأعور بن عمرو بن معاوية
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: ذو الغرة الجهني ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2468) lists Dhu al-Ghurra al-Juhani, also said to be al-Hilali. 'Abdullah ibn Ahmad (Zawa'id al-Musnad), al-Baghawi and Ibn al-Sakan transmit, via Abu Ja'far al-Razi from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, his hadith that a bedouin asked the Prophet about praying in camel pens and he said no. Ibn Hajar notes the chain runs through the weak 'Ubayda ibn Mu'attib, and that al-A'mash and Hajjaj ibn Artat attributed the hadith instead to al-Bara' ibn 'Azib or Usayd ibn Hudayr. The entry also links him to the name Ya'ish al-Juhani. No death year is given.
research_evidence: ذو الغرّة الجهنيّ: ويقال الهلالي. روى عبد اللَّه في زيادات المسند، والبغويّ، وابن السّكن، من طريق أبي جعفر الرازيّ، عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، عن ذي الغرّة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: رافع بن سنان الأنصاري الأوسي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2538) lists Rafi' ibn Sinan al-Ansari al-Awsi, kunya Abu al-Hakam, grandfather of 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Hakam. Abu Dawud transmits, through 'Abd al-Hamid from his father from his grandfather, the hadith that he accepted Islam while his wife refused. Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam traces his descent to al-'Atabun ('Amir ibn Tha'laba). No death year is given.
research_evidence: رافع بن سنان الأنصاريّ الأوسيّ، أبو الحكم، جد عبد الحميد بن جعفر بن عبد اللَّه بن الحكم بن رافع بن سنان

full_name_ar: ربيعة بن عامر بن بجاد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2614) lists Rabi'a ibn 'Amir ibn Bijad al-Azdi, also said to be al-Du'ali, counted among the people of Palestine; Abu 'Umar (Ibn 'Abd al-Barr) names his grandfather al-Had. Ahmad, al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim transmit his hadith, via Yahya ibn Hassan of Jerusalem, in which he heard the Prophet say 'Cling to Ya Dha al-Jalal wa al-Ikram'. Abu 'Umar says only this one hadith is known from him. No death year is given.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2842) lists Zuhayr ibn 'Amr al-Hilali, a settler of Basra. Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi narrated from him and, per al-Azdi, was his only transmitter; al-'Askari says he had a house in Basra. Al-Baghawi knows only his hadith of the warning (al-indhar), which Muslim recorded, though Ibn al-Sakan reports al-Bukhari did not authenticate it because direct hearing was not stated. No death year is given.
research_evidence: زهير بن عمرو الهلالي: نزيل البصرة. روى عنه أبو عثمان النّهديّ، قال الأزديّ: تفرد أبو عثمان عنه

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 2857) lists Ziyad ibn al-Harith al-Suda'i (also said Ziyad ibn Haritha, but al-Bukhari holds al-Harith is correct). He has a long hadith on the story of his conversion containing 'whoever gives the adhan gives the iqama', transmitted in full by Ahmad and by the Sunan compilers through al-Ifriqi, a chain Ibn al-Sakan questioned; other routes go through 'Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Maysara and Ziyad ibn Nu'aym. Ibn Yunus says he was a well-known man who settled in Egypt. No death year is given.
research_evidence: زياد بن الحارث الصّدائي: بضم المهملة، وقيل زياد بن حارثة. قال البخاريّ: والحارث أصح

full_name_ar: سعد مولى أبي بكر ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3228) lists Sa'd, mawla of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, also called Sa'id, though Ibn 'Abd al-Barr says Sa'd is better known and more correct. Ibn Majah transmits his hadith (and al-Tirmidhi alludes to it), narrated by al-Hasan al-Basri from him, that he used to serve the Prophet, concerning eating dates two at a time. Al-Baghawi has another hadith by the same route calling him 'mawla of the Messenger of God', which Ibn Hajar explains is because he served the Prophet, not because he was the Prophet's freedman. No death year is given.
research_evidence: سعد، مولى أبي بكر الصّديق: ويقال سعيد، والأول أشهر وأصحّ. قاله ابن عبد البرّ. روى حديثه ابن ماجة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: سعيد بن أبي راشد ( رضي الله عنه

hadith_narrated.url: http://qaalaRasulAllah.com/hadith.php?ID=5&Rows=2&SID=5062&head=Sunan Ibn Majah [Narrated by Sa'id bin Abi Rashid سعيد بن أبي راشد]

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3264) lists Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid, said to be of Jumah; Ibn Hibban says he was a companion. Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan, Ibn Abi Dawud, Ibn Shahin and Ibn 'Adi (al-Kamil) transmit, via 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit from him, the hadith 'In my community there will be earth-swallowing, transformation and pelting', with a weak chain. Ibn Hajar thinks the Sa'id ibn Abi Rashid who was the teacher of 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym and narrated the report of Caesar's envoy is a different person. No death year is given.
research_evidence: سعيد بن أبي راشد: يقال إنه جمحيّ. قال ابن حبّان: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: سفيان بن أسيد ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3314) lists Sufyan ibn Asad, or Usayd, al-Hadrami, whom Ibn Abi Khaythama, Ibn Abi 'Asim and others counted among the companions. His hadith, transmitted via Baqiyya from Dubara ibn Malik al-Hadrami, from his father, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from his father, is that he heard the Prophet say: 'It is a great betrayal to tell your brother something he believes while you are lying to him.' No death year is given.
research_evidence: سفيان بن أسد بفتحتين أو أسيد- بوزن عظيم- الحضرميّ. ذكره ابن أبي خيثمة وابن أبي عاصم وغيرهما في الصّحابة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: سلمان بن عامر بن أوس ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3368) lists Salman ibn 'Amir ibn Aws ibn Hujr al-Dabbi, a companion who narrated from the Prophet and settled in Basra. His niece Umm al-Ra'ih (al-Rabab bint Sulay'), his grandson 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Bishr, and Ibn Sirin and his sister Hafsa bint Sirin narrated from him. Ibn Hajar notes disagreement over his death: some say in 'Umar's caliphate, al-Sarifi says in 'Uthman's, but the correct view is that he lived into Mu'awiya's time. No exact death year is given.
research_evidence: سلمان بن عامر بن أوس بن حجر بن عمرو بن الحارث بن تيم بن ذهل بن مالك بن بكر بن سعد بن ضبّة الضّبيّ
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: سلمة بن قيس/ نفيع ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The shamela.ws narrator card (drawing on Tahdhib al-Kamal of al-Mizzi, al-Kashif of al-Dhahabi, and Tahdhib al-Tahdhib and Taqrib al-Tahdhib of Ibn Hajar) lists Salama ibn Qays, also said to be Ibn Nafi', Ibn La'im or Ibn La'i ibn Qudama, al-Basri al-Jarmi, a companion who came as a delegate to the Prophet, and father of 'Amr ibn Salama. No death year is given.
research_evidence: سلمة بن قيس، وقيل: ابن نفيع، وقيل: ابن لائم، وقيل: ابن لائي بن قدامة ... البصري، الجرمي ... له صحبة ووفادة على النبي

full_name_ar: سنين أبو جميلة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3531) lists Sunayn, Abu Jamila al-Sulami, also said to be al-Damri, whose father's name is given as Waqid by Ibn Hibban. Al-Bukhari transmits via al-Zuhri from Abu Jamila that he performed hajj with the Prophet. Ibn Sa'd places him in the first generation of the tabi'un and says he has hadiths; al-'Ijli calls him a trustworthy tabi'i. No death year is given.
research_evidence: سنين بالتّصغير، أبو جميلة السّلميّ. ويقال الضّمري. وقيل اسم أبيه واقد، حكاه ابن حبان
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: سلام بن عمرو اليشكري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3352) lists Sallam ibn 'Amr, whose companionship is disputed; Ibn Hibban placed him among the tabi'un. Ibn Manda transmits via Abu 'Awana from Abu Bishr from Sallam ibn 'Amr, described as one of the Prophet's companions, the hadith 'Dogs are impure except the hunting dog'; Ibn Manda holds that Shu'ba's version, in which Sallam narrates from an unnamed companion, is correct. Ahmad's Musnad and al-Bukhari's al-Adab al-Mufrad carry another text through the same chain. The al-Isaba entry does not state the nisba al-Yashkuri. No death year is given.
research_evidence: سلّام: بالتثقيل، ابن عمرو. مختلف في صحبته. وقد ذكره ابن حبّان في التّابعين. وروى ابن مندة، من طريق أبي عوانة، عن أبي بشر، عن سلّام بن عمرو
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: شريح الحجازي له صحبة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3900) lists Shurayh ibn Abi Shurayh al-Hijazi; al-Bukhari and Abu Hatim say he was a companion. Al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh transmits via 'Amr ibn Dinar and Abu al-Zubayr, who heard Shurayh, a man who met the Prophet, say 'Everything in the sea is (already) slaughtered'; al-Bukhari cites it as a ta'liq in the Sahih, and al-Daraqutni and Abu Nu'aym transmit it via Ibn Jurayj from Abu al-Zubayr as a marfu' report, though Abu Nu'aym indicates the preserved version is mawquf. No death year is given.
research_evidence: شريح: بن أبي شريح الحجازي. قال البخاريّ وأبو حاتم: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: الشريد بن سويد ( رضي الله عنه

hadith_narrated.url: http://qaalaRasulAllah.com/hadith.php?ID=4&Rows=1&SID=5084&head=Sunan an-Nasa'i [Narrated by al-Shryd bin Swyd al-Thqfy الشريد بن سويد]

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 3911) lists al-Sharid ibn Suwayd al-Thaqafi; Ibn al-Sakan says he was a companion, his hadith is among the Hijazis and he settled in Ta'if. Most call him Thaqafi, though some say he was of Hadramawt origin allied to Thaqif. His original name is said to have been Malik, and he was called al-Sharid because he fled from al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba after the latter killed his Thaqafi companions, a story related by al-Waqidi. Muslim and others transmit from him via his son 'Amr ibn al-Sharid, and al-Bukhari has a suspended report from him. No death year is given.
research_evidence: الشريد بن سويد الثقفيّ ... عمرو بن الشريد عن أبيه
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: صخر بن وداعة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4074) lists Sakhr ibn Wada'a al-Ghamidi, who settled in Ta'if. His hadith 'O God, bless my community in its early mornings' is transmitted by the Sunan compilers and Ahmad; only 'Umara ibn Hadid narrated from him. No death year is given.

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4412) lists 'Amir ibn Shahr al-Hamdani, also called al-Bakili or al-Na'iti, with the kunya Abu Shahr or Abu al-Kunud. He has a hadith in Abu Dawud transmitted by al-Sha'bi from him, with a longer version in Abu Ya'la, recounting his coming to the Prophet and mentioning his tribe Hamdan and the Negus. No death year is given.
research_evidence: عامر بن شهر الهمداني ويقال البكيلي، بالموحدة وكسر الكاف الخفيفة، ويقال الناعظي، بالنون والمهملة والظاء المعجمة، أبو شهر

full_name_ar: عباد بن شرحبيل اليشكري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4484) lists 'Abbad ibn Shurahbil (also Sharahil) al-Yashkuri, of Banu Ghubar of Yashkur. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Abi 'Asim transmit his hadith with a sound chain via Abu Bishr: being hungry, he entered a garden in Medina and ate some grain, the owner beat him and took his cloak, and the Prophet rebuked the owner for neither teaching him when ignorant nor feeding him when hungry. The entry cites al-Tabarani's al-Awsat, Usd al-Ghaba and al-Isti'ab. No death year is given.
research_evidence: عباد بن شرحبيل، ويقال شراحيل، اليشكري، ثم الغبري من بني غبر، بضم المعجمة وفتح الموحدة الخفيفة، ابن يشكر

bio: The shamela.ws narrator record lists 'Abdullah ibn Sa'd with the nisbas al-Ansari, al-Fihri, al-Umawi, al-Harami, al-'Abshami and al-Tamimi, ranks him as a Companion (sahabi), and gives his places of residence as Damascus and Homs. The record draws on al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba, Tahdhib al-Kamal, Ikmal Tahdhib al-Kamal, Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, Taqrib al-Tahdhib and al-Kashif. Al-Isaba (shamela.ws/book/9767/2529, entry 6622) adds that Ibn 'Abd al-Barr separated 'Abdullah ibn Sa'd al-Azdi from 'Abdullah ibn Sa'd the uncle of Haram ibn Hakim, but Ibn Hajar holds they are one person. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن سنان بن نبيشة بن سلمة ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The shamela.ws narrator record gives his full lineage as 'Abdullah ibn Sinan ibn Nubaysha ibn Salama ... al-Muzani and ranks him as a Companion according to Ibn Hajar, al-Dhahabi and al-Mizzi. Muhammad ibn Sa'd says he settled in Basra and had descendants there; Khalifa ibn Khayyat says he had companionship (suhba); Ibn Hajar says he is counted among the Companions. He was the father of 'Alqama ibn 'Abdullah al-Muzani and died during the caliphate of Mu'awiya (no exact year given). Sources cited include Tahdhib al-Kamal, Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, Taqrib al-Tahdhib, al-Kashif and al-Isaba.
research_evidence: عبد الله بن سنان بن نبيشة بن سلمة بن سلمان بن النعمان بن صبح بن مازن بن حلاوة بن ثعلبة بن ثور بن هذمة بن لاطم بن عثمان المزني
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الله بن غنام ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 4900) gives his lineage as 'Abdullah ibn Ghannam ibn Aws ibn Malik ibn 'Amir ibn Bayada al-Ansari al-Bayadi. Al-Baghawi, quoting Ahmad ibn Salih, affirms he had companionship (suhba). He has one hadith in Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Nasa'i on what to say in the morning; some transmitters corrupted his name to Ibn 'Abbas or 'Abd al-Rahman, which Abu Nu'aym and Ibn Hajar call an error. The shamela.ws narrator record (narrator/3841) also ranks him as a Companion per Ibn Hajar and al-Dhahabi (al-Kashif, Tahdhib al-Kamal). No death year is given.
research_evidence: عبد اللَّه بن غنّام بن أوس بن مالك بن عامر بن بياضة الأنصاري البياضي. قال البغويّ، عن أحمد بن صالح: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

bio: Ibn Hajar's al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba (entry 5499) quotes al-Bukhari that 'Adi ibn Zayd al-Judhami settled in Medina and narrated from the Prophet; al-Baghawi mentioned him without citing the hadith. bio: The shamela.ws narrator record names him Kinaz ibn al-Husayn ibn Yarbu' al-Ghanawi, kunya Abu Marthad, a Companion who fought at Badr. Abu Hatim al-Razi says he had companionship; Ibn Hajar calls him a Badri Companion; al-Dhahabi says Badri. Sources cited: al-Jarh wa-l-Ta'dil, Taqrib al-Tahdhib, al-Kashif and al-Isaba.

full_name_ar: المنذر بن عائذ بن المنذر بن الحارث ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The hdith.com narrator encyclopedia names him al-Mundhir ibn 'A'idh ibn al-Mundhir ibn al-Harith ibn al-Nu'man ibn Ziyad ibn 'Asr, known as al-Ashajj, with the nisbas al-'Asari, al-'Abdi and al-'Umani, a Companion who settled in Basra and Bahrain. Al-Mizzi describes him as the chief of his people who came to the Prophet in the delegation of 'Abd al-Qays; Abu Hatim al-Razi says he had companionship; Ibn Hibban and Ibn Hajar affirm his Companion status. Nine hadiths are recorded from him. Sources cited: Tahdhib al-Kamal, Ikmal Tahdhib al-Kamal, al-Isaba and al-Jarh wa-l-Ta'dil. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: مهاجر بن قنفذ ( رضي الله عنه
bio: The tarajm.com entry gives his given name as 'Amr ibn Khalaf ibn 'Umayr ibn Jud'an al-Qurashi al-Taymi, known by the names al-Muhajir and Qunfudh (al-Muhajir ibn Qunfudh), with the kunya Abu Sasan among his students. He is a Companion and hadith narrator; the Prophet called him 'truly a muhajir' when he came as a Muslim after being tortured by the polytheists, though another report says he embraced Islam at the conquest of Mecca. He served as chief of police under 'Uthman, lived in Medina and Mecca, settled in Basra and died there. Hudayn ibn al-Mundhir al-Raqashi and his grandson Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhajir narrated from him. Sources cited: al-Isti'ab, Usd al-Ghaba, al-Isaba, Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd and Mu'jam al-Sahaba (Ibn Qani'). No death year is given.

full_name_ar: نصر بن دهر بن الأخرم ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Nasr bin Dahr (also written Dhahr) bin al-Akhram al-Aslami was a companion of the Prophet, as was his father Dahr. The page recounts, from al-Isaba and Usd al-Ghaba, that he was present on the march to Khaybar when the Prophet asked Amir bin al-Akwa to recite verses, and that he took part in the stoning of Ma'iz. Al-Baghawi says he settled in Medina and has two narrations; Ibn Abd al-Barr notes his grandson Abdullah bin al-Haytham bin Nasr transmitted from him. No death year is given.

bio: Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Sabra al-Ju'fi, kunya Abu Khaythama, was a companion counted among the Kufans; his father Abu Sabra was Yazid bin Malik bin Abdullah al-Ju'fi. Al-Sha'bi and his son Khaythama bin Abd al-Rahman narrated from him. No death year is given.

full_name_ar: مصعب بن الزبير بن العوام الأسدي القرشي
bio: Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam al-Asadi, son of the companion al-Zubayr, served as governor of Basra (686-691) and earlier of Medina for his brother the caliph Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr during the Second Fitna. In 687 he defeated al-Mukhtar al-Thaqafi in Kufa and, according to al-Waqidi and Abu Mikhnaf as cited in the article, executed some 6,000-7,000 of Mukhtar's supporters. He was defeated by the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik at the Battle of Maskin in October 691 and killed at Dayr al-Jathaliq by Za'ida ibn Qudama al-Thaqafi. The article draws on Wellhausen (1927) and Dixon (1971) among others.

full_name_ar: أمية بن عبد الله بن خالد
bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (al-Mizzi) gives him as Umayya bin 'Abdullah bin Khalid bin Asid bin Abi al-'Is bin Umayya bin 'Abd Shams, a Qurashi Umayyad of Mecca and brother of Khalid bin 'Abdullah. He narrated from 'Abdullah bin 'Umar bin al-Khattab; those who narrated from him include 'Abdullah bin Abi Bakr, 'Atiyya bin Qays al-Shami, Abu Ishaq 'Amr bin 'Abdullah al-Sabi'i, Muhammad bin Muslim al-Zuhri and al-Muhallab bin Abi Sufra. 'Abd al-Malik bin Marwan appointed him governor of Khurasan; al-'Ijli graded him a trustworthy Medinan tabi'i. The entry records that he died in the year 87 (سنة سبع وثمانين، فيها مات أمية بن عبد الله بن خالد بن أسيد). Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah transmitted his hadith.

He narrated from 'Utba bin Muhammad bin al-Harith bin Nawfal and from his mother, who narrated from Maymuna; Sufyan bin 'Uyayna, 'Abd al-Malik bin Jurayj and 'Umar bin Sa'id narrated from him. Ishaq bin Mansur reports Yahya bin Ma'in graded him trustworthy (ثقة). Al-Nasa'i transmitted one hadith from him. No death year is given.
research_teachers: 'Utba bin Muhammad bin al-Harith bin Nawfal
research_evidence: منبوذ بن أبي سليمان ويقال: ابن سليمان المكي يقال: اسمه سليمان ومنبوذ لقب غلب
dod_s: c. 753 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (al-Mizzi) lists al-Walid bin 'Abdullah bin Abi Mughith, a client (mawla) of Banu 'Abd al-Dar, from the Hijaz. He narrated from Muhammad bin 'Ali bin Abi Talib (Ibn al-Hanafiyya) and Yusuf bin Mahak al-Makki; Ibrahim bin Yazid al-Khuzi, 'Ubaydullah bin al-Akhnas, Muhammad bin 'Abdullah bin 'Ubayd and Ma'qil bin 'Ubaydullah al-Jazari narrated from him. Yahya bin Ma'in (via 'Uthman al-Darimi) graded him trustworthy and Ibn Hibban listed him in al-Thiqat. Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah transmitted his hadith. No death year is given.
research_teachers: Muhammad bin 'Ali bin Abi Talib (Ibn al-Hanafiyya)

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (al-Mizzi) lists Yasar, Abu Najih al-Thaqafi al-Makki, father of 'Abdullah bin Abi Najih and client of al-Akhnas bin Shurayq. He narrated (mursal) from the Prophet and from Huwaytib bin 'Abd al-'Uzza, Khalid bin Hakim, Rabi'a al-Jurashi, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas and 'Abdullah bin 'Abbas among others; his son 'Abdullah, 'Abd al-Rahman bin Khudayr al-Ansari and 'Amr bin Dinar narrated from him. Ahmad bin Hanbal (via al-Maymuni) called him one of the best of God's servants; Yahya bin Ma'in and Abu Zur'a graded him trustworthy (ثقة). 'Amr bin 'Ali and Abu Bakr bin Abi 'Asim state he died in the year 109 (مات سنة تسع ومئة). Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i transmitted his hadith.

full_name_ar: يزيد بن عبد المزني
bio: Entry no. 7026 in al-Mizzi's Tahdhib al-Kamal describes him as Yazid ibn Abd al-Muzani, a Hijazi. He narrated from the Prophet the report on the aqiqah ('yuaqq an al-ghulam wa la yumass ra'suhu bi-dam'); Ayyub ibn Musa al-Qurashi narrated from him. full_name_ar: أسلم بن عمران أبو عمران التجيبي
bio: Tarajm.com, quoting al-Dhahabi's Tarikh al-Islam, records Abu Imran al-Tujibi al-Misri (given there as Aslam ibn Yazid) as a freedman of Umayr ibn Tamim who narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, Uqba ibn Amir, Umm Salama and Safiyya; Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, Yazid ibn Abi Habib and Abdullah ibn Iyad narrated from him. He is graded thiqa and was declared trustworthy by al-Nasa'i; death is given as 91 AH / 709 CE in Egypt. The patronymic 'ibn Imran' used in this dataset appears in al-Shashi's Musnad heading 'أسلم بن عمران أبو عمران التجيبي عن أبي أيوب' (shamela.ws/book/13066/1260); kunya, nisba and teacher Abu Ayyub match.

He narrated from his father Sinan, his grandfather Wahb ibn Munabbih, Mujahid ibn Jabr, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn and al-Bakhtari ibn Hilal; among those who narrated from him are al-Hakam ibn Aban al-Adani, Sharahbil ibn Abd al-Karim al-San'ani, al-Mu'afa ibn Imran al-Mawsili and his son Abd al-Mun'im. No death year is stated. Match is on name plus nisba al-San'ani; the dataset gives no further lineage.

bio: Entry no. 890 in al-Mizzi's Tahdhib al-Kamal: Jami' ibn Matar al-Hubati al-Basri, cited by al-Bukhari (Raf' al-Yadayn), Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i. He narrated from Burayd ibn Abi Maryam al-Saluli, Abu Ru'ba Shaddad ibn Amr al-Qaysi, Alqama ibn Wa'il ibn Hujr, Mu'awiya ibn Qurra al-Muzani and Umm Kulthum bint Thumama; among those who narrated from him were Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, Bakr ibn Isa al-Rasibi and Abu Umar al-Hawdi. Critics said 'ma ara bihi ba'san', 'thiqa' and 'la ba'sa bihi'. The entry gives his death as 128 AH or, per another report, 127 AH (conflicting, so left null here).
